newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Sonae seen posting 18-20 bln esc profit.
newsitem.headline: Sonae seen posting 18-20 bln esc profit.

text.p: Sonae Investimentos, Portugal's largest private sector company, should post a net consolidated profit of 18-20 billion escudos on Monday when it announces its results, analysts estimate.

The figure, which incorporates hefty extraordinary gains, is up from 12.9 billion escudos in 1995. The results will be the last for the group in its present form as wood company Sonae Industria and property and media concern Pargest were split off from the start of 1997.
"The net profit should be about 19 billion escudos, including extraordinaries," said Rosa Cunha of Espirito Santo Research (ESR).
At the end of 1996, the group carried out two significant asset sales -- 49 percent of Sonae Imobiliaria and 25 percent of SM, the company controlling shopping centre CascaiShopping.
Banco Finantia's Tiago Felix was also looking for around 19 billion escudos of net profit, adding that the current share price was discounting such a result.
"We believe that at the current levels, the company is fairly priced," he said.
The dividend is seen at 150-160 escudos, in line with last year's 150 escudos.

Sonae Investimentos' stock has gained some 11 percent since the start of the year on optimism over the benefits of the split which was regarding as making the company more transparent and easier to analyse, traders say.
After touching a high for the year of 5,930 escudos, the stock had slipped back to reach 5,500 on Friday against 4,970 at the end of last year.
